key_insight: Thermodynamic consistency in biochemical reaction-network inference can be encouraged by penalizing detailed-balance violations instead of explicitly enforcing Wegscheider constraints.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more scalable and numerically stable way to calibrate physically grounded reaction models, especially when Bayesian inference and complex network topologies make direct constraint handling difficult.
method: Infer network parameters with a penalty term that discourages detailed-balance violations.
Avoid explicit cycle identification and reparameterization needed for direct Wegscheider enforcement.
Apply and test the approach on both a single-cycle toy network and a PKA-calcineurin signaling model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that unconstrained inference fit the data but violated thermodynamic constraints, while the proposed penalty preserved data agreement and produced posterior samples that approximately satisfied detailed balance.
watch_item: Because the constraint is enforced approximately rather than exactly, the penalty strength must be tuned carefully to balance physical consistency against fit quality and sampling performance.
paper_title: Enforcing Thermodynamic Consistency in Parameter Optimization and Bayesian Inference of Biochemical Reaction Networks
